The *Piṇḍola Sutta* (Ud 4.6, PTS Ud 42) is the sixth discourse of the fourth chapter (*Meghiyavagga*) of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. The sutta depicts the venerable elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja seated in meditation, providing the narrative setting for an inspired utterance (*udāna*) by the Buddha. While modern scholarly literature frequently examines Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja's role in the Vinaya, his reputation in narrative literature, and the subsequent cult devoted to him across East Asia, none of the retrieved secondary literature focuses specifically on this brief discourse.
